title: Exact $1/4$ mean-rung population and $\sqrt{2}$ continuum revival-time ratio in the anti-Jaynes--Cummings vertex at $f_\star=\sqrt{\bar n+1}$
abstract: At atomic resonance the Jaynes--Cummings (JC) vertex of a single bosonic mode coupled to a two-level emitter is blind to $f=ω/λ$ at zero detuning and Kerr; the anti-Jaynes--Cummings (AJC) vertex is not. We show that the mean-rung excited population of the AJC block equals exactly $1/4$ at $f_\star=\sqrt{\bar n+1}$, while the JC population at the same point is $1/2$. The Poisson-averaged packet value at $\bar n=16$ is $0.24650$, within $3.5\times 10^{-3}$ of the exact value, with the deviation reproduced by $-\bar n/[16(\bar n+1)^2]$. At $f_\star$ the modulation depth of the AJC inversion is $1/2$ and the relative sensitivity of the continuum revival-time ratio $r=t_R^{\rm AJC}/t_R^{\rm JC}$ is maximal with value $1/(2\sqrt{\bar n+1})$. Full diagonalization on $2(n_{\max}{+}1)$ states confirms the analytic values. The $1/4$ value can be generated by Floquet-engineered counter-rotating coupling provided that the static transverse rate satisfies $g_0\ll g_1$. Parameter translations for an ideal trapped-ion blue sideband and a flux-tunable circuit-QED coupler are reported.
summary: This paper analyzes the anti-Jaynes-Cummings (AJC) coupling vertex, showing that its mean-rung excited population reaches an exact value of $1/4$ at a specific frequency $f_\star$. The authors establish this as a robust diagnostic tool by comparing it to the JC vertex and mapping the required conditions onto experimental setups like trapped ions and circuit QED. It provides a deep theoretical understanding of quantum coupling dynamics in these systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the differences between the Jaynes-Cummings (JC) and anti-Jaynes-Cummings (AJC) coupling vertices in a cavity QED setting, using the AJC vertex as a differential measurement tool.
main_result: The mean-rung excited population in the AJC vertex reaches an exact value of $1/4$ at a specific frequency $f_\star=\sqrt{ ar{n}+1}$, and the continuum revival-time ratio $r$ is maximized at this point.
method: The analysis combines analytic derivations based on Hamiltonian diagonalization with comparisons to packet-averaged values and full Hilbert-space simulations.
model_or_system: The system models a two-level emitter coupled to a single bosonic mode, analyzed using both the JC and AJC Hamiltonians. The theory is mapped onto physical platforms like trapped ions and circuit QED couplers.
key_observables: Mean-rung excited population (AJC vs. JC), continuum revival-time ratio ($r=t_R^{m AJC}/t_R^{m JC}$), and the contrast $C(f)$.

It then derives key analytic results concerning the population and revival times at the special point $f_\star$. Finally, it translates these theoretical findings into concrete parameter mappings for trapped-ion and circuit QED implementations.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly quantitative theoretical framework for using subtle differences between two related quantum coupling regimes (JC vs. AJC) to perform precise measurements in cavity QED, linking fundamental theory to specific experimental platforms.
